title: Randomized Controlled Trial on Dimensional Changes Following Immediate Post-Extraction Implant Placement With a Gap ≥2 mm, With or Without Bone Regeneration Using a Xenograft.
official: Randomized Controlled Trial on Dimensional Changes Following Immediate Post-Extraction Implant Placement With a Gap ≥2 mm, With or Without Bone Regeneration Using a Xenograft.
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine whether bone grafting is necessary for bone healing following immediate dental implant placement in adults aged 18 years or older who require extraction and replacement of a posterior tooth (premolar or molar) and have a gap of at least 2 mm between the implant and the surrounding buccal bone.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does placing a dental implant without a bone graft result in bone healing that is not clinically worse than placing an implant with a bone graft?
* Are there differences in bone thickness, bone height, and changes in the width of the jawbone between the two treatment approaches? Researchers will compare immediate dental implant placement with a bone graft to immediate implant placement without a bone graft to evaluate bone healing and changes in the surrounding bone over 24 months.

Participants will:

* Undergo tooth extraction and immediate placement of a dental implant, with or without a bone graft, according to random group assignment.
* Receive a permanent implant-supported dental crown approximately 10 weeks after surgery.
* Attend scheduled follow-up visits over 24 months for clinical examinations and assessment of implant health.
* Undergo dental X-rays, three-dimensional cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans, and digital intraoral scans to evaluate bone healing and changes in the tissues surrounding the implant.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients aged 18 years or older, partially edentulous, requiring replacement of a single tooth in the posterior region (premolar or molar) by means of immediate post-extraction implant placement.
* Presence of a post-extraction socket with a horizontal buccal gap ≥2 mm, confirmed intraoperatively after implant placement.
* Intact buccal bone wall (without dehiscence or fenestration), clinically confirmed after tooth extraction.
* Clinical conditions allowing adequate primary implant stability to be achieved (≥35 Ncm).
* Patients classified as ASA I or ASA II according to the American Society of Anesthesiologists classification.
* Patients who understand the nature of the study, sign the informed consent form, and agree to attend all scheduled follow-up visits over the 24-month study period.
* Availability to undergo the radiographic assessments (CBCT and periapical radiographs) required by the study protocol.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients classified as ASA III or ASA IV, or with uncontrolled systemic diseases that may interfere with bone healing or clinical follow-up.
* Presence of uncontrolled acute infection at the extraction site that contraindicates immediate implant placement.
* Buccal bone defects involving loss of the buccal bone wall (dehiscence or fenestration).
* Need for additional regenerative procedures other than those established in the study protocol.
* Treatment with medications that may significantly affect bone metabolism (e.g., intravenous bisphosphonates or immunosuppressive agents).
* Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
* Heavy smoking (according to the threshold defined in the study protocol).
* Inability to comply with the scheduled follow-up visits or complete the required assessments.
* Any condition that, in the investigator's judgment, may compromise adherence to the study protocol, data validity, or patient well-being.
